title: POC economics, credits slab and benchmarking sprint
summary: Initial POC scoping focused on pilot economics (credit slab), benchmark sprint plan, success criteria for Blueleaf Health's clinical summarization workload, and the commercial path to enterprise contracting. Customer is risk-averse on PHI and wants VPC/private controls; buyer timeline linked to Q2 budget review. Agreed to run a 2-week benchmarking sprint with defined test harness and cost envelope; Redwood to propose credits slab and pilot terms; procurement to follow after successful benchmarks.
transcript:
Header: 2025-01-17 15:30 PST — Duration: 48m — Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Maya (Redwood SE), Ethan (Blueleaf CTO), Priya (Blueleaf Head of ML), Liam (Blueleaf Procurement), Sara (Eng Mgr)

[00:00] Jordan (Redwood): hey everyone, thanks for carving out time. quick roundtable — i'll run through the agenda then hand to maya for the benchmark details.
[00:12] Ethan (Blueleaf): morning, yeah, thanks. we got three items — cost, timeline, and security. those are make or break.
[00:22] Maya (Redwood): great, i'll jump in on the benchmarking approach, but first jordan, do you want to cover pilot economics?
[00:28] Jordan (Redwood): sure — so high level, our standard pilot we call a credits slab. it's basically prepaid credits that draw down per-token or per-embedding. for a typical 2 week sprint we usually propose a small slab and then we true-up after the benchmarks. but — and this is important — we can set caps and alerts so you don't unexpectedly burn.
[00:44] Priya (Blueleaf): how granular is that? like can we put a hard cap per-day or per-route? we have a lot of small internal routes for internal summarization and a single external API for clinicians.
[00:56] Jordan (Redwood): yes, per-route throttles and daily caps are configurable. also you can pin a model variant to a route so the cost profile is predictable.
[01:08] Liam (Blueleaf): procurement question — what's the minimum commitment for a pilot? legal usually needs a statement of work or an MSA.
[01:16] Jordan (Redwood): for pilots we usually do a short SOW plus our standard pilot terms — no long-term financial commitment beyond the credits slab. if you convert post-pilot to dedicated or enterprise, that's when we negotiate term and SLAs.
[01:28] Ethan (Blueleaf): PHI is a big concern. are you offering VPC/private plane for the pilot or do we have to do it on hosted?
[01:36] Maya (Redwood): good question. technically, we can run an isolated environment — for pilots we often use a dedicated tenancy within our hosted stack with encryption/KMS controls, but we also support Private/VPC if you need full network isolation. note: private deployments add lead time.
[01:52] Sara (Blueleaf): how much lead time are we talking about for private?
[01:56] Maya (Redwood): typically 4-6 weeks for a Private deployment depending on approvals and HSM/KMS onboarding; dedicated tenancy in hosted for pilots can be stood up in days.
[02:08] Priya (Blueleaf): ok, that helps. for the benchmark itself — our core workload is clinical note summarization. average input length ~3.2k tokens, target output ~150-250 tokens. throughput expectation is low concurrency but strict latency for clinician UI: 95th p95 under 800ms ideally.
[02:28] Maya (Redwood): got it. we'll profile both latency and cost. plan: run a 7-10 day benchmark sprint with three model variants (base open model, quantized variant, and a run-time optimized variant) across representative test set. measure: p50/p95 latency, tokens/sec, and cost per 1k generated tokens.
[02:48] Jordan (Redwood): on the commercial side we propose credits slab tiers: small (50k credits), medium (200k), large (500k). each maps to an estimated token budget depending on model choice. for a 2-week 10k-record run we'd recommend the medium slab but we'll give a proper estimate after Maya's workload sizing.
[03:06] Ethan (Blueleaf): what do you define as a credit? can you convert to a dollar figure upfront so procurement can justify?
[03:12] Jordan (Redwood): yes, credits are effectively pre-paid units; we'll translate to a USD-equivalent in the SOW. for transparency we'll show a per-token rate and a projected burn table.
[03:22] Liam (Blueleaf): procurement needs cancellation terms and liability language. if we do PHI, we need BAA and SOC2 type II evidence.
[03:30] Jordan (Redwood): we have a standard BAA for healthcare customers and SOC2 reports — will share the security pack. for pilot SOW we can include the BAA as a signed addendum.
[03:42] Priya (Blueleaf): one more note on accuracy: clinical summarization errors are sensitive. success criteria for us is a human-AI F1-ish metric plus clinician qualitative pass rate >85% on a 50-sample set.
[03:56] Maya (Redwood): perfect — we'll incorporate those success criteria into the benchmark checklist. we'll also run a small set of hallucination tests and a regression harness.
[04:08] Jordan (Redwood): timeline-wise, if we kickoff next Monday we can have the benchmark plan and test harness ready in 3 business days and start the sprint the following week. contract/procurement can run in parallel.
[04:20] Ethan (Blueleaf): timeline is tight because of Q2 budget lock on 2025-04-01. if pilot completes by end of Feb we can present ROI in March.
[04:30] Jordan (Redwood): understood. we'll prioritize rapid deck and benchmark definitions.
[04:36] [05:00] Maya (Redwood): technical bits — we need a representative dataset (de-identified) and an API test harness. we'll simulate KV cache warmed and cold start scenarios; also run both streaming and non-streaming generation to see latency profiles. note: "K-V cash" was mentioned in earlier run, sometimes the transcript has K-V cash — but we mean KV cache.
[05:18] Priya (Blueleaf): we can provide a de-id set of ~1k notes, sampling across specialties. is that volume sufficient?
[05:24] Maya (Redwood): yes, that plus a 50-sample clinician review set. we will run three model configs and instrument token counts, latency, and quality.
[05:34] Jordan (Redwood): commercial guardrails we propose for this pilot: 1) one-time credits slab (medium) with per-route caps; 2) a 30-day refund window pro-rated if pilot canceled early; 3) usage alert thresholds at 50/75/90% of credits; 4) success-based conversion credit — if you convert to committed capacity within 60 days we apply 25% of unused pilot credits toward the first month.
[06:02] Liam (Blueleaf): that conversion credit helps procurement. what's the definition of "convert"? signed contract and committed monthly spend?
[06:10] Jordan (Redwood): yes, executed order form for Dedicated or Private with minimum first-month payment. we'll define details in the SOW.
[06:18] Ethan (Blueleaf): do you support on-prem for compliance reasons? we mentioned earlier, but curious on costs and IR.
[06:24] Maya (Redwood): on-prem is supported but usually a multimonth engagement; costs depend on hardware you provide vs Redwood-managed hardware. for pilots we recommend hosted dedicated tenancy with strict encryption.
[06:36] [06:50] Priya (Blueleaf): any known performance regressions when using quantized models for clinical summarization? we want to avoid quality loss.
[06:58] Maya (Redwood): quantized models can reduce cost with modest accuracy delta; we'll measure ROUGE/clinical-F1 and surface examples. we often run a quality threshold — if quantized variant fails >10% of samples, we drop it from production recommendations.
[07:12] Jordan (Redwood): ok let's talk deliverables: redwood will deliver a benchmark results packet, a cost burn report, and a recommended deployment matrix (hosted/dedicated/private) plus an SOW with credits slab and pilot terms.
[07:26] Ethan (Blueleaf): procurement wants a clear contracting path — who do we loop in from your side?
[07:32] Jordan (Redwood): i'll be primary AE contact for contracting, maya will handle technical acceptance. legal and finance contact will be cc'd on the SOW.
[07:40] Liam (Blueleaf): after benchmarks if we like results we want a 60-90 day pilot extension possibility and clear renewal pricing.
[07:48] Jordan (Redwood): noted — we'll include extension options and price bands in the SOW.
[07:54] [08:10] Maya (Redwood): quick note about instrumentation — please include P95 traces for both streaming and blocking calls, we'll also surface per-token breakdown and cache hit rates. the more telemetry you provide the better we can optimize.
[08:26] Priya (Blueleaf): ok, sounds good. any risks on your side for meeting the p95 latency?
[08:32] Maya (Redwood): we will run a brief pre-benchmark sanity test; if anything looks off we can adjust model variants or batching policies. for clinician UI we can also use synchronous streaming to keep perceived latency low.
[08:44] Jordan (Redwood): wrap-up — recap next steps and owners.
[08:48] Ethan (Blueleaf): quick interjection — who handles data deletion/retention at end of pilot?
[08:54] Jordan (Redwood): we have on-demand data wipe and retention policies; we'll include the data handling annex in the security pack.
[09:02] Priya (Blueleaf): great.

Notes: occasional transcription artifacts ("Redwood Dedikated" appears in auto-text) — watch for those while reading the attached transcript.

Closing: timeline alignment — aim to start benchmark plan work on 2025-01-20; pilot sprint target window 2025-01-27 to 2025-02-07. procurement review during Feb, decision window by 2025-03-10.
